step2.ptxt: The back guide monitor system consists of the following parts.

item.ptxt: Turns the television camera assembly ON/OFF according to the reverse signal input from the park/neutral position switch assembly.

Combines the rear view image input from the television camera assembly with images calculated based on vehicle condition information such as the steering angle signal, and displays it on the display screen.
When the back guide monitor screen or diagnosis screen is displayed, operation is performed using the touch panel on the display screen.
Draws each adjustment screen used on the diagnosis screen.
If a back door open signal is received, camera optical axis adjustment is canceled.
Stores each adjustment value set on the diagnosis screen.

entry.ptxt: Captures images behind the vehicle and sends the video signal to the navigation receiver assembly.
Sends the vehicle speed signal to the navigation receiver assembly.
Sends the reverse signal to the navigation receiver assembly when the shift lever is in R.
Sends the steering angle signal to the navigation receiver assembly via CAN communication.
Instrument Panel Junction Block Assembly (Main Body ECU)
Sends the back door open/closed signal to the navigation receiver assembly via CAN communication.

step3.ptxt: The back guide monitor system uses CAN communication for data communication between the navigation receiver assembly and each ECU.

If there is a problem in the CAN communication line, the navigation receiver assembly outputs a CAN communication malfunction DTC. (Check using the TaSCAN diagnostic tool screen and the diagnosis screen of the navigation receiver assembly) (For the procedure, refer to and )
If a CAN communication malfunction code is output, repair the communication line malfunction, and troubleshoot the back guide monitor system with data communication in a normal condition. (see )
Each CAN communication line has a specified length and routing, and temporary measures or repairs using bypass wiring, etc. cannot be performed. (see )
The back guide monitor system uses AVC - LAN for communication between components.
The master component of the AVC - LAN is the navigation receiver assembly.
The navigation receiver assembly contains a resistor necessary for communication transmission (60 to 80 Ω between terminals TX+ and TX-).

If a malfunction such as a short in the communication line, short to +B or short to GND occurs in the AVC - LAN circuit, communication is interrupted, and the back guide monitor system and HDD navigation system do not operate normally.
The video signal from the television camera assembly is input to the navigation receiver assembly via an analog signal line (vehicle wire harness).
The video signal input from the camera is processed by the navigation receiver assembly and drawn on the display as the back guide monitor system screen.

The back guide monitor system has a diagnosis function that allows checking the status of each signal input to the navigation receiver assembly, as well as registration settings, adjustment and checks of the back guide monitor system.
